daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

President Prabowo warned that groups seek to change Pancasila ideology and fragment the nation during a speech at the Complex Warfare Course closing ceremony. The president urged military personnel to study history and avoid repeating past mistakes, emphasizing the need to protect Indonesia's unity. He also addressed perceptions that SMA Taruna Nusantara appears elitist but serves to identify talented students, as he inaugurated the school's new campus in Cimahi.

  • The Supreme Court granted a lawsuit annulling Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka's high school equivalency certificate, ordering it destroyed and declared invalid, though legal experts debate whether this affects his vice presidential status.
  • PDIP and PKS have established communication channels to address the Gibran diploma controversy together.
  • DPR Speaker urged a transparent probe as 20 corporations were named suspects in forest fires, with a legislator calling for tougher penalties for offenders.
  • A DPR legislator stated the Asset Forfeiture Bill could return funds to victims of fraudulent investment schemes.
  • The KPK named Dedi Congor a new suspect in the Customs and Excise corruption case, adding to his existing suspect status at the National Police.
  • A former Customs official asked that the term "commander" in a bribery case not be associated with his superiors, while another official expressed regret for tarnishing the Customs name after 30 years of service.
  • The Deputy Home Affairs Minister clarified statements about high-performing local governments receiving Rp 1 trillion in relation to the MBG program.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Indonesia and Uruguay established a framework for cultural cooperation, marking a new bilateral agreement between the two nations. The agreement aims to strengthen cultural ties and exchange programs between Indonesia and the South American country. Meanwhile, former Vice President Jusuf Kalla remembered former Japanese Prime Minister Yasuo Fukuda as a friend of Indonesia while conveying condolences.

  • South Korea seeks nuclear energy ties with Indonesia as Seoul and ISDS invited students to propose ideas for strengthening bilateral relations.
  • The KP2MI agency stopped prospective migrants from joining mercenary forces abroad.
  • The Foreign Ministry stated there is no information on Indonesian victims in a train accident in Spain.
  • A Banten arts group carried a cultural diplomacy mission through theater performances in Pakistan.
  • President Prabowo attended the closing ceremony of the Complex Warfare Course at Pusdiklatpassus special forces training center.

Other

Food prices rose sharply with red chili reaching Rp 96,200 per kilogram and chicken eggs hitting Rp 29,350, monitoring data showed. The increases come as inflationary pressures continue to affect household budgets across the country. The rupiah remained stuck around Rp 18,100 with domestic political tensions adding pressure to the currency.

  • BPJS Kesehatan issued a clarification on viral claims that PBI health insurance for deciles 9-10 would be deactivated on November 1, while Health Minister stated the president is determined to advance the health insurance program.
  • The BGN authority suspended 6,097 SPPG beneficiaries who failed to report daily fund usage.
  • Jakarta will launch another vehicle tax penalty waiver program, while the governor plans to send 10 urban village heads abroad for learning visits.
  • The MSMEs Ministry seeks accelerated distribution of KUR microcredits, while Central Papua will train 300 farmers to boost coffee quality.
  • The Attorney General's Office raided offices at Menara Batavia in connection with the Toba Pulp Lestari case, while a DPR member urged corporations to bear forest fire recovery costs rather than the state budget.
